verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 4.1% to $180.6B and operating income grew 8.3% as its U.S. stores gained share — but a $294M paper loss on its investment stakes, versus a gain a year ago, left headline profit down 4.4% at $5.3B.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — net sales up 5.0%, comparable sales up 4.6%, eCommerce up 20%.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — net sales down 0.7% in dollars but up 5.7% in constant currency, led by China, Walmex and Canada; growth was hurt by the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 5.7%, or 7.1% excluding fuel, with comparable sales up 6.8% excluding fuel and eCommerce up 24%.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Sam's Club membership fees plus advertising (Walmart Connect in the U.S. grew 24%) and other income.

opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office.

otherDetail: Interest of $602M, net, plus a $294M loss on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves. A year ago that investments line was an $813M gain.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $5,254M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $5,425M, of which $171M belongs to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: Walmart keeps just $2.91 of every $100 — but on $180.6B of quarterly revenue that is still $5.3B. The stores themselves earned 8.3% more than a year ago; a $294M paper loss on investment stakes held the headline profit down.

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 8.3% to $7.9B — twice the pace of sales — as the gross margin rate improved 53 basis points, led by Walmart U.S., membership income grew, and eCommerce economics got better.
takeaways.title: Stores earned faster than sales

takeaways.text: A $294M loss on equity and other investments, versus an $813M gain a year ago, turned a strong store quarter into a 4.4% decline in headline profit. Adjusted EPS, which strips the loss out, was $0.66 versus GAAP EPS of $0.65.
takeaways.title: Paper losses cut the headline

takeaways.text: Walmart raised its annual dividend 13% to $0.94 per share — its largest increase in over a decade — after generating $36.4B in operating cash flow for the full year.
takeaways.title: Dividend raised 13%

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $294M loss — mostly fair-value moves on equity investments (a year ago it was an $813M gain). Adjusted EPS of $0.66 excludes a $0.02 net-of-tax loss from these items.

A $99M gain from opioid-related legal matters — proceeds from settlement of a shareholder derivative lawsuit, recorded in Corporate and support — boosted reported operating income. Adjusted operating income of $7,760M excludes it.

Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale shifted on the calendar, which moved some International sales into Q3 and held back Q4 — International net sales fell 0.7% in dollars but rose 5.7% in constant currency.

sources.label: Form 10-K, fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
